subject: Burst tolerance & prompt-mix probe for reserved fleet sizing
messages:
From: Lucia Ramos <lucia@brightflux.ai>

Cc: BrightFlux Ops <ops@brightflux.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved fleet sizing — burst tolerance / prompt mix details

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team liked the predictable SLOs and the KV cache stuff. We're exploring a reserved (dedicated) fleet for our inference workloads and need a quick sizing sanity-check from you and your solutions folks. High-level info below; happy to add telemetry exports if useful (attached a small CSV sample).

What we need from you: can Redwood help size a committed pool that hits our p99 latency targets during frequent bursts (we see 3–4x baseline RPS for ~90s windows) without massive over-commit? Also want recommendations on instance mix and whether session affinity / hot-KV caching will materially reduce required GPUs for our workload.

Key context (approx):
- Typical model family: open Llama-2-family fine-tuned for retrieval-augmented generation (seq len 1024)
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg response tokens: 560 (longer outputs ~5% of requests are 2k+ tokens)
- Baseline concurrent sessions: 450 (steady), peak bursts: up to 1.8k concurrent for ~60–120s, 2–3x of baseline across business-critical hours (US East)
- Allowed p99 latency for short responses: 300ms; for long-form generation (2k tokens) we can tolerate up to 3.5s
- We do a lot of streaming output to the browser (token-by-token) and reuse session KV caches for 70% of sessions
- Expected monthly token volume: ~1.6B tokens (forecasting modest growth)

Attached is a small sample of burst traces (burst_profile.csv) and a prompt sample (prompt_samples_v2.txt). Happy to hop on a quick call. Do you need a full request log?

Thanks,

Lucia
Lucia Ramos
Head of Platform
BrightFlux

Hi Lucia — thanks for the sample and the clear context. This is the sort of traffic profile our dedicated sizing flow was built for. Quick read-through notes below, then a couple of clarifying questions so Dev can run a conservative sizing pass.

High-level: from the numbers you shared, we expect two levers will drive required GPU counts: sustained concurrency (baseline 450) and the 60–120s bursts to ~1.8k. With 70% KV reuse and streaming, we can often reduce token compute by ~15–30% relative to cold runs, but that depends on affinity and cache warm-rate.

Clarifying asks (can reply inline or in the attached worksheet):
1) Do bursts align with particular endpoints (e.g., search vs. long-form generation)? If bursts are dominated by short responses, we can optimize batching and prefer higher-frequency smaller-capacity instances.
2) What percentage of requests open a new session vs reuse an existing session? (you noted 70% reuse — is that by session id or per-user?)
3) Any hard SLA constraints for p50/p90 besides the p99 numbers?

Plan: Dev will sketch two committed pool options — conservative (handles sustained + bursts with <10% queuing at p99) and lean (assumes 60% KV reuse and accepts modest queuing under the largest bursts). We'll include recommended GPU SKUs and an ops playbook (auto-burst, canary fallback to hosted).

If OK, I'll schedule a 30-min sizing call Weds (your timezone) with Dev and Marissa to align on the mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved fleet sizing — burst tolerance / prompt mix details

Hi Lucia — quick technical follow-ups so we size to the right constraints. I'll run a first-pass estimate after these answers.

Questions:
- Peak RPS during the 60–120s bursts (not just concurrent sessions) — do you have a 1s/5s sample?
- Do you stream tokens client-side for the long outputs or buffer server-side and then chunk? Streaming increases tail latency sensitivity for sending partial tokens but reduces memory pressure per request.
- Model quantization: are you planning int8 or fp16 serving for the committed fleet?
- Cold-starts: what fraction of requests hit uncached weights (model swapping / multi-tenant checkpoints)?
- Retry behaviour: do clients retry aggressively on 503s? This changes the effective burst intensity.

If you can paste a 5–10 minute burst trace (timestamp,RPS,avg tokens) or grant our SRE read-only access to a short window in your observability (we can ingest a small sample), that'll let us produce a tighter GPU SKU recommendation. I'll also output two costed options (dedicated A and B) with expected p99 queuing and suggested autoscale/burst policies.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — answers inline below, and I'm pasting a short 10-minute burst snippet (also shared in Drive):

- Peak RPS in that burst window: ~950 rps at the 5s sample, avg tokens during peak ~680 (prompt+response). Concurrent sessions measured at ~1800 due to long-lived streaming.
- Streaming: we stream tokens to the client as they are generated (websocket) for all outputs.
- Quantization: plan today is fp16 in our experimental clusters; we'd prefer int8 in production if it preserves the output quality.
- Cold-starts: negligible — we keep a warm pool for active models, but we do checkpoint swap for edge experiments (~5% of requests hit a swapped model).
- Retries: clients backoff aggressively; retry rate observed ~2% during failures.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/brightflux-traffic

Let us know if you want more granular telemetry. We can also open a narrow read-only window to our monitoring if that helps sizing.
